same_choices: Un-save is the same button re-clicked; it replays the save animation in reverse (reverse morph / reverse spatial displacement) rather than a separate delete UI
Save is optimistic: the animation plays immediately on click and silently reconciles / rolls back on server failure
The interaction starts on pointerdown (~0-16ms) so fast saves never flash a loader
A small transient in-flight marker appears only during the network round-trip and disappears on ack (skeleton shimmer / inline teal dot) — same behavioral role and lifecycle
Saved state is signalled with a green-teal accent (mint / teal); the glyph's color turns teal-green on save
Confirmation is deliberately kept off the label/toast path — no 'Saved!' toast; a lightweight persistent state signal is used instead
Un-save is the same button re-clicked; it plays the exact save animation backward (reverse morph / reverse scrub)
Save is optimistic and reconciles silently on failure by reversing
The interaction fires on pointerdown for ~0 perceived latency
Saving animates a fill rising up into the bookmark glyph (clip-path tide rise / amber fill wipes up) — same 'fill fills the icon from the base' experience
The bookmark glyph deforms in shape as part of the state change (pennant droop / ribbon fold), not just a color swap
Dark toolbar surface with a single saturated accent (mint on ink / amber on slate)
The confirmation/feedback element sits beneath the button (underline bar+count / 'Saved' tooltip chip) rather than only inside the glyph
Core motion moves the icon DOWN and seats it into a recessed container at the button's lower edge (drops into a slot / tucks into a pocket) — same spatial displacement into a lower receptacle
Physical-object metaphor: the icon behaves as a tangible thing that settles/tucks and then pops back out
Un-save is the same button re-clicked, playing the settle/tuck in reverse (token pops up / ribbon lifts out)
Save is optimistic and reconciles silently on failure
The interaction fires on pointerdown for ~0 perceived latency
prefers-reduced-motion collapses the animation to an instant snap/swap plus the state change
aria-pressed toggles saved/unsaved for accessibility

enumeration_overlap: Un-save 'same-button/same-click toggle' (01, 03) and 'replay same anim reversed in place' (02)
Un-save reverse-animation option: 'click-again reverse morph' (01) / 'reverse spatial displacement' (02) / 'reverse scrub' (03)
Saved cue filled glyph: 'filled icon' (01) / 'outline->solid fill' (02) / 'filled glyph' (03)
Saved cue color-only: 'color swap' (01) / 'color shift only' (02) / 'color-only swap' (03)
Saved cue 'underline bar' as an option in both 01 (spatial anchor) and 03 (persistent cue)
notes: All three share one interaction skeleton (optimistic, pointerdown start, same-button reverse-animation toggle) and their per-concept options tables overlap heavily, especially on un-save, pending, and saved-cue choices. They diverge mainly on motion primitive and confirmation modality; 02 and 03 additionally converge on the same 'move down into a pocket/slot' metaphor.
